- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to under-forecast; increase forecast slightly to align with upward momentum.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33), model often over-forecasts; reduce forecast to match downward pressure.
- Model frequently over-estimates short-term spikes (e.g., +5–10% above recent high) and under-estimates subsequent mean reversion; apply a 1–2 day lag correction after sharp rises.
- In periods of high volatility or sentiment divergence, model tends to over-react to recent price movements; dampen forecast sensitivity to last 3–5 days.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often under-predicts the final 5–7 days; adjust final 5–7 days upward by 1–3% to reflect sentiment-driven tail momentum.
- When sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to misalign with the cycle’s midpoint; shift forecast toward the sentiment-weighted average of recent 7–10 days.
